\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Boolean derivative]
\lean{FABL.booleanDerivative}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p014-b010,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p161-b004
}
\label{FABL.booleanDerivative}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube}
For a natural number $n$, a function $f:\bbr_2^n\to\bbr_2$, and $y\in\bbr_2^n$, the Boolean
derivative of $f$ in direction $y$ is the function sending each $x\in\bbr_2^n$ to
$f(x)+f(x+y)$, with addition in $\bbr_2$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Product expansion of a monomial]
\lean{FABL.anfMonomial_add}
\label{FABL.anfMonomial_add}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfMonomial}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the coordinates $\mathbin n$, and let
$x,y\\in(\\bbr/2\\bbr)^n$. The monomial indexed by $S$ evaluated at the coordinatewise
sum $x+y$ equals the sum, over all subsets $T\\subseteq S$, of the monomial indexed by
$T$ at $x$ times the monomial indexed by $S\\setminus T$ at $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative of a finite-field monomial]
\lean{FABL.booleanDerivative_anfMonomial}
\label{FABL.booleanDerivative_anfMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.anfMonomial_add, FABL.booleanDerivative}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let
$y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. For every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$, the Boolean derivative of the
monomial $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ in direction $y$ equals $\displaystyle\sum_{T\subsetneq
S}\left(\prod_{i\in T}x_i\right)\left(\prod_{i\in S\setminus T}y_i\right)$ in
$\mathbb{F}_2$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let $y$ be
a point of the Boolean cube over the two-element field. The algebraic degree of the
Boolean derivative in direction $y$ of the monomial on $S$ is at most $|S|-1$, with
subtraction taken in the natural numbers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative expansion in algebraic normal form]
\lean{FABL.booleanDerivative_eq_sum_anfMonomial}
\label{FABL.booleanDerivative_eq_sum_anfMonomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfEval, FABL.anfEval_anfCoeff, FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.booleanDerivative}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f\colon\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$, and let
$y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. For each subset $S$ of the coordinates, define
$a_S=\displaystyle\sum_{T\subseteq S} f(1_T)$ in $\mathbb{F}_2$, where $1_T$ is the
vector whose coordinates in $T$ are $1$ and whose other coordinates are $0$. Then, for
every $x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$,
$f(x)+f(x+y)=\displaystyle\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}a_S\bigl(m_S(x)+m_S(x+y)\bigr)$,
where $m_S(z)=\prod_{i\in S}z_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a Boolean derivative]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_booleanDerivative_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p161-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p162-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p162-b002
}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_booleanDerivative_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.algebraicDegree_le_iff, FABL.anfCoeff, FABL.anfMonomial, FABL.booleanDerivative, FABL.booleanDerivative_eq_sum_anfMonomial, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_booleanDerivative_anfMonomial_le, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_finset_sum_le, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube over the
two-element field to that field, and let $y$ be any point of the cube. The algebraic
degree of the Boolean derivative of $f$ in direction $y$ is at most the algebraic degree
of $f$ minus one, where subtraction is in the natural numbers.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree under domain translation]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_domainTranslate}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_domainTranslate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.domainTranslate, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_comp_affineEquiv, FABL.𝔽₂}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ be a Boolean function, and let
$z\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. The function $x\mapsto f(x+z)$ has the same algebraic degree as
$f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Derivative of a translated Boolean function]
\lean{FABL.domainTranslate_booleanDerivative_eq_two_translates}
\label{FABL.domainTranslate_booleanDerivative_eq_two_translates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.booleanDerivative, FABL.domainTranslate, FABL.domainTranslate_apply}
\difficulty{4}
For any natural number $n$, let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^n\to\mathbb{F}_2$ be a Boolean function
and let $y,y'\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Translating the Boolean derivative of $f$ in direction
$y+y'$ by $y$ gives the function $x\mapsto f(x+y)+f(x+y')$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a sum of translates]
\lean{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_add_translates_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p162-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p162-b002
}
\label{FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_add_translates_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.F₂BooleanFunction, FABL.F₂Cube, FABL.domainTranslate_booleanDerivative_eq_two_translates, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_booleanDerivative_le, FABL.functionAlgebraicDegree_domainTranslate}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional cube over $\mathbb{F}_2$ whose
algebraic degree is $d$, and let $y,y'$ be points of that cube. The function $x\mapsto
f(x+y)+f(x+y')$, with addition over $\mathbb{F}_2$, has algebraic degree at most
$\max(d-1,0)$.
\end{theorem}
